After you fly a plane in DCS you feel like you could jump right into the real thing and fly it. The level of detail is extraordinary, the graphics are beautiful, the combat is exhilarating. With that said, the game is what is is, a simulator. It's not cheap, you'll buy a HOTAS, trackIR or VR, as well as planes; It's not easy and it doesn't hold your hand, you have to LEARN to play it. DCS is in a league of its own. It's the closest you can reasonably get to learning how to fly a fighter jet short of becoming a fighter pilot. It's not "fun" in the traditional sense, but it is infinitely enjoyable. It's spending hours reading manuals, learning maneuvers, and getting your equipment set up just right. It's more about learning than playing.

Most of the negative reviews I've seen are about the price. People have to understand that this is a very niche product: this isn't a game so much as it is work. When a high-quality product has a small userbase, that means the price will be exorbitantly high; and the people who like these types of sims will have no problem paying it. Many DCS players have $1,000+ in flight sim hardware and a high end PC--do you really think a $70 plane they could spend a thousand hours learning to fly is going bother them?

This is an expensive hobby, so if you just want to have fun at a reasonable cost, you will hate DCS. But if you're fascinated with flight and love a challenge, this is the thing for you.

*DCS World* (Digital Combat Simulator) is a standout game on Steam because of its unmatched realism and attention to detail in flight simulation. Whether you're piloting a fighter jet, helicopter, or ground vehicle, DCS offers an incredibly immersive experience with accurate physics, clickable cockpits, and true-to-life systems that mirror real military equipment. The game also supports VR, enhancing immersion even further for players who want the sensation of truly being in the cockpit. With frequent updates, a strong modding community, and a wide variety of aircraft and missions, DCS provides endless hours of strategic gameplay, making it a top-tier choice for aviation and military enthusiasts.

While DCS modules are expensive when not on sale, no other flight sim comes close in terms of quality and enjoyment. I recommend picking up Flaming Cliffs 3 if you are a new player who has tried the free to play elements and feel ready to invest more.

I strongly recommend a basic HOTAS for this game. It makes a huge difference, and I really wouldn't try using M&K controls.

If you want to try face tracking, which you will, there is an App on iPhone and Android called "SmoothTrack" that is only $10 and surprisingly good. Just make sure you have good lighting on your face when using this though.

An alternative to TrackIR is DelanClip, which is just as good as TrackIR at a fraction of the cost (albeit with a slightly less "Plug in and play" first time setup). They are UK-based so distant countries will get longer post times but mine arrived 4 days after ordering, despite being warned it could take longer! I have the wired version since I hate wireless but they do have a well reviewed wireless option.

Some people say "oh no is so hard to learn all the stuff there", well they are missing the point here, it ain't a game, it's a sim. So, the steep learining curve on the "clickable cockpit" modules is the most rewarding thing of the whole platform.

Sure, you can strap yourself into an f-15 and start killing bandits in a couple of hours, but the real pleasure, the real immersion, the real deal is in the learing and the feeling of locking a ground target with a maverick 7nm away (it may seem easy, but it ain't!) or dropping a CBU-105 and watch the earth burn or dodging a sam launch almost kissing the ground with your wing is an adrelanie rush hard to match in pc gaming.

If you ain't a real life pilot (like me), well this is the next best thing.

Heck I have dropped a few Hornets in the drink after catapult shot due to pilot error. No Joke. No VR helmet and doing swell... now the VR is on my list but am totally enjoying learning how our pilots actually get it done. 4 attempts and still not pulled off the Air to Air refueling, no big deal yet. 20 miss approaches and 2 crashes but did pull off CV landing. Then you learn to unhook from cable, learn your tight turn switch for the front wheel, learn where to park, rearm, refuel, get clearance to takeoff, pick the catapult, line up, get hooked up, check all your switches and gauges, set takeoff weight to trim, go to after burn, wiggle all the surfaces and PRAY! If you have the time, willing to learn and love to fly combat in any form, HOPE TO SEE YA! Not one second upset purchasing the F-18 and will be adding to my Hanger.

- Play the tutorial and some free content
- Buy a couple of modules
- Practice takeoff, landing and navigation for hours to get used to my new modules
- Watch more youtube videos to learn about my sensors and weapon systems
- Play against bots on easy settings to get used to combat
- Play against bots on harder settings to get used to realist combat
- FInally feel ready to join a multiplayer game
- Join a server, jump in my Su-27, load some missiles and take off
- Fly low towards bulls with my radar off and EOS on to reduce my chances of getting detected
- Get shot down by some guy in a helicopter

10/10
